properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Donegal Township, Washington County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/21/2025 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Donegal Township, Washington county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/21/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8221962
Permit API: 125-29142
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/21/2025
Comments: On 02/21/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/21/2024 Range Resources Representative, Derek Zofchak, reported an approximately 25 to 30-gallon release of reused water off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representatives, Derek Zofchak and Denny Furmanek, were on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Furmanek and Mr. Zofchak informed the Department that that the release was discovered today (02/21/2025) at 10:55 am, that the quantity released was approximately 25 to 30 gallons, and that remediation efforts had already begun on the impacted area. The source of release was determined to be damaged secondary containment. The secondary containment had been damaged by a truck tire and the fluids on containment overtopped the containment berm and continued off an adjacent duck pond and onto the pad aggregate. Conductivity probe calibrated on 02/21/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-The area impacted by the release was observed. The area appeared to measure approximately 150 ft in length by 35 ft in width. Pooled fluid with a sheen was observed throughout the area. The damaged secondary containment was observed. It was made known that a crew was on site to repair the damaged containment. A vac truck was observed on site removing pooled fluids in the impacted area and on containment (Photos 3-5).-Field conductivity screening was conducted immediately in front of a large, gray electrical box. Over Range (greater than 20 ms/cm) field conductivity readings were observed (Photos 6-8).-Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 7.21 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 9-12).-The extent of the impacts was observed where a non-elevated field conductivity screening of 1,432 s/cm was observed (Photos 13-14).-Remediation efforts were in progress at the time of inspection. Operators were observed scraping off impacted aggregates with heavy machinery (Photos 15-17).-A roll-off box arrived on site during the inspection. It was stated that the impacted material would be placed in the roll-off box and that waste manifests would be provided to the Department (Photo 18).Determination:Violations issued.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/14/2023
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 8158480
Permit API: 019-22800
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Prospect Borough
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/14/2023
Comments: At the time of inspection, 4 Patton wells remain partially drilled on the Coretsky well pad. On 9/12/2022, the plugging certificates for the four Coretsky wells (Permit Nos. 37-019-22741, 37-019-22742, 37-019-22798 and 37-019-22799) were received. The Patton C 2H gas well, Permit No. 37-019-22800 has 9-5/8" intermediate casing installed to 1886 feet according to a partial well record (Photo 6). This was accomplished in April 2019. An Unconventional Alteration Permit (Authorization No. 1402359) was issued on 9/08/2022. This permit has expired and well has not yet been completed. Plugged Coretsky wells and partially drilled Patton wells are surrounded by cattle fence and steel plates are placed over wells. The pressure gages above the steel plates all read zero psi and the valves are open. There are no well tags to identify locations of Patton wells (Photo 1). Production equipment on well pad consists of four separator units (Photo 2) and six 400 bbl production water tanks (Photo 3). No pipeline has been run to pad (Photo 4). Department records indicate that operator is submitting production reports that show well has been spud and Mechanical Integrity Assessment Reports indicate in comments section that well is a Regulatory Inactive well. A violation for failure to plug a well upon abandoning it ( OGA3220(A)) was issued during inspection.

Approximately 15 gallons of produced water was spilled onto the well pad off containment. The following was observed during inspection: At the time of the inspection, I observed that SPSI appeared to have finished remediation. Approximately 60 x 60 feet of contaminated area was excavated. I observed multiple wet spots within the remediated area. No elevated conductivity was observed around the remediated/excavated and initial spill area (Photo 1-7).Logan Dominick from EQT stated in an email received on 12/05/2024 regarding spill location and updated description:On 12/3/24, we had a water truck off loading at the Comtec stands on the Gregor pad, supporting the frac. During the offloading process, the pump on the Comtec stand malfunctioned, causing the pump to back feed pressure into the truck and caused fluid to be released from the PRV on the truck. Once Environmental was able to investigate further, it was determined that the quantity was right around 1 bbl. This release is being put through Act 2. All remediation was completed the same day and consultant took confirmatory samples. Photos from Logan Dominick were included within the email, post-remediation and pre-remediation (Photo 8-10).Violations are being issued for: 78a.54, 91.34(a), CSL 301, CSL 307(a),SWMA 301, and 78a.57(a)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/07/2025 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Cogan House Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/07/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8244479
Permit API: 081-22038
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/07/2025
Comments: On August 7, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection to a reported spill at the Expand Energy Elly May Well Pad. On August 6, 2025 at 1638, Expand Energy reported to the spill hotline that fluid with elevated conductivity was found outside of the containment on the well pad surface. Expand Energy estimated that approximately 32 gallons was leaked outside of the containment. Upon arrival at the well pad, Expand was vacuuming out the suspected containment causing the leak to the well pad. DEP screened the conductivity of the free liquid that had pooled next to the secondary containment and resulted in 2,570 uS/cm. The area where the free liquid had pooled next to the secondary containment was about 25 feet by 15 feet. After the containment was completely emptied and moved to determine the extent of the leak, a small hole was found in the plastic liner of the containment. Expand then vacuumed up the free liquid on the well pad surface. Mike Deming with Expand Energy arrived shortly after the free liquid had been vacuumed from the well pad surface. Mr. Deming explained that Expand had recently washed down the timber mats in this secondary containment. So the water leaking from containment was a mixture of wash down water and rainwater. Mr. Deming said that Expand expects to have a piece of machinery at the well pad by noon to begin excavating the contaminated soil in the area of impact. Mr. Deming said that Creston Environmental was scheduled to delineate the spill and confirm the remediation of the spill. DEP left the site prior to Expand beginning the excavation of the area of impact. At 1445, Mr. Deming called DEP to report the area of impact had been excavated. In an email provided by Mr. Deming, the area of excavation was approximately 19' by 29' with an average depth of 4". The conductivity of the soil after scraping the contaminated soil from the area of impact was less than 450 uS/cm. Mr. Deming said approximately 8.75 tons of contaminated soil was placed in a lined dumpster. Based on the amount of contaminated soil removed and the calculation completed for the amount of liquid that soil could hold, 32 gallons is the volume leaked from containment onto the well pad surface. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 have been noted. Due to the immediate remediation of the spill the violations are considered corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 2019-10-11
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 865002
Permit API: 033-26887
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Lawrence Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-11
Comments: Doug Kepler of Seneca Resources called and reported a mixed brine/water spill of 1 barrel to the Department on October 10, 2019 at 1600. Mr. Kepler stated that crews were onsite cleaning up the spill as he was reporting it to the Department. Chapter 78a.66(b)2 states that all spills and/or releases should be reported to the Department within 2 hours after detecting or discovery of the release. I conducted an incident site inspection on October 11, 2019 with Kyle Kline of Seneca Resources at D-17 COP-B well pad. According to Mr. Kline, a well tender was onsite the previous day plunging well (033-26887) when a float got stuck on the separator. Pressure built up over time causing fluids to be released through the rupture disc located on the GPU separator. During my inspection I viewed the separator, the impacted area adjacent to the seperator, and the roll off box containing the impacted materials. I conducted field screenings using a soil probe randomly throughout the excavated area. Screenings ranged from 0 uS/cm- 220 uS/cm. Approximately 2-3 cubic yards of impacted materials were viewed inside the lined roll-off box. Please note, that Seneca Resources sent the Department an email on October 15, 2015 revising the initial spill volume from 1 barrel to 0.5-0.75 barrels of produced fluids released. This information was revised based off the well tenders report of claiming that the plunger system brings 1-1.5 barrels of produced fluids with each cycle. According to the well tender about 50% of the fluids went to the tank and the other 50% was released to the pads surface. Based off the Departments inspection, the Department concurs with this spill volume correction. Violations have been noted and have been immediately corrected.

Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative

Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/14/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Broadleaf Holdings (01-115) on 7/14/2025 at 0630 hours. The weather ranged from mid-70s to mid-80s degrees throughout the day. The inspection was conducted in response to a report of a well control incident occurring on the 7H well which resulted in a release of produced fluids. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390569 is tied to the release in CTS.According to Repsol, at ~1830 hours on 7/13/2025 a pressure issue on the 7H well caused the uncontrolled release of produced fluid up the casing[s] to the pad surface. Efforts to control pressure and prevent the escaping fluids have failed so far. Secondary containments were overtopped and fluid has and continues to escape the pad surface. A temporary berm was constructed along the northwestern edge around the western corner of the pad, below the fill slope, to collect fluids (photos #3 to 5). The "corner" berm below the fill slope was said to be completed around 0000 hours on 7/14/2025. Numerous gravel berms were constructed on the pad surface to help prevent fluids from escaping the pad surface but are failing in numerous spots. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed sheet flowing from numerous areas along the southwestern edge of the pad (see photo #8 for example). Fluid observed in the western corner of the stormwater control basin was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned a reading of >19.99mS/cm. ~1000 hours: A Repsol representative onsite indicated that larger pumps were en route to catch up on fluid collection that is being pooled on the western corner of the well pad (photo #9). According to Repsol, the pumps being brought in should be able to catch up on the fluid that is pooled on the surface.A secondary berm/trench was constructed below the first "corner" berm below the fill slope sometime throughout the day. A break in the first berm was dug to allow fluid collected to flow into the secondary berm. The secondary berm is flowing fluid into the stormwater control basin onsite (see photos #10-12).Fluid was able to reach the stormwater control basin shown in photo #7. The DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the basin which was field measured at >19.99mS/cm (Sample #0983-510).A third (tertiary) berm/trench was later constructed below the secondary berm and was built into the stormwater control basin. The short side wall of the basin was removed to allow for excess fluid build-up in the basin to collect in the third berm. The secondary and tertiary berms are utilized to relieve hydrostatic pressure from the "corner" berm. Fluids field measured at >19.99mS/cm were observed on the pad surface, in the constructed berms, in the pad's stormwater channels and in the stormwater control basin. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were observed directly down-gradient of the well pad, below the constructed "corner" berm and along the installed surface waterline. Soils field measured at >4.00mS/cm were also observed along the surface waterline in the field adjacent to the pad (photo #13).Repsol identified and initiated the screening and sampling of nearby water supplies as required by 25 Pa. Code 78a.66b(4).Based on the findings of this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API #015-23892 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 25 Pa. Code 78a.54, SWMA 301 and Clean Streams Law 401. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.55(f) is cited against API #015-23892 as immediately corrected.I departed the well pad at 1430 hours.

Violation ID: 8175462
Permit API: 065-24911
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Winslow Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/12/2024
Comments: On 2/8/2024, Diversified staff discovered that the brine tank at API 065-24911 had overflowed when the line pressure dropped and the well was able to unload to the small 50 bbl tank. This spill was reported to the Department. The on-site estimate of the lost production fluid was approximately 5 bbl. During the 2/9/2024 INCDT inspection report (Inspection ID 3709744) it was documented that the brine tank had been drained and disconnected, and contaminated soil had been excavated and placed on plastic sheeting. Plastic will also be used to cover the contaminated soil to protect it from precipitation until the material is removed. Due to the loose conditions of the soil at this site, it appears that the contamination has traveled deep under the former tank location and does not appear to have a large lateral zone of impact. An Act 2 clean up will be conducted at the site, and Moodys is the anticipated consultant for this remediation activity. Due to this spill and the unpredictable nature of this well, a larger brine tank will likely be attached to the well after remediation has been completed.Today, I completed a FUI inspection. Diversified was still onsite removing contaminated soil. Weather permitting, they plan on completing the clean up on Wednesday, 2/14/2024.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/16/2026
Comments: On March 16, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regard to a release reported to the Department on 3/15/2026 (CTS 395839). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nick Reda.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. Wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, 9H, 1H,10H,11H,12H, and 14H) appeared equipped for production with well tags present. Mr. Reda stated they are currently swapping out equipment to complete flowback operations on the 13H.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks and GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Reda guided the Department to the location(s) of the reported release. According to Mr. Reda the release occurred on 3/15/2026. He stated the release was caused by a scrubber malfunction on a third-party water truck. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of produced water released to the graveled access road.The Department observed the location(s) of the release and remediation. It appeared the area of the release was split into two different sections of the access road. Mr. Reda said due to the malfunction of the scrubber on the water truck, the release occurred only on the steep portions of the access road. Therefore, the release began approximately halfway down the access road, ceased as the truck reached a level area, and then continued to release on another steep section towards the bottom of the access road.Upon inspection of where the release began, the Department observed an area where impacted material was excavated from the access road (photos 12-13). According to Mr. Reda, the release in this area of the access road was about 150 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Small puddles of rainwater were observed in this section of the access road. Conductivity readings of 0.49mS, 0.24mS, and 0.43mS, were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained in the gravel on the side of the access road near the well pad entrance (away from the spill and heavy vehicle traffic). Prior to leaving the site, the area of excavation was backfilled with clean gravel (Photos 23-24).Upon inspection of where the release continued near the bottom of the access road, the Department observed fresh gravel (Photo 17). Mr. Reda stated the impacted material had been removed and the area of excavation had been backfilled. Mr. Reda stated the release in the area of the access road was about 180 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Conductivity readings of 0.12mS, 0.15mS, and 0.23mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained.Mr. Reda stated all impacted material was placed into 3 roll-off boxes (photos 21-22) and would be disposed of properly. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the observed release as it appeared to be remediated in accordance with current regulations (78a66).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-09-17 to Cabot Oil & Gas Corp in Auburn Twp, Susquehanna county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Cabot Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-17
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 863494
Permit API: 115-22557
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-17
Comments: The Department was on-site in response to the report of a spill incident of more than (5) gallons of diesel based drilling mud that occurred on 9/16/19 at 17:05 hours. The weather conditions are sunny skies with a light breeze, and temperatures in the upper 60's. Remediation of the impacted area affiliated with the spill was in progress. Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA is the Cabot subcontractor delineating the extent of the impact via the use of a photoionization detector (PID) meter to determine the presence of volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds. H&P Flex Rig 259 is the drilling rig on the location. The current drilling depth of the M Powers 12H well is (4,351.59) feet. Cassidy Moyer, DEP WQS and I initially met with Mike Stansfield, Drilling Engineer of Cabot in the site office/company man trailer. Mr. Stansfield provided the following information relevant to site activities and the spill incident. "The rig is on the M Powers 12H well. Remediation of this well is in progress. The 4H and 8H wells will be drilled to total depth (TD). All other wells on the pad have been drilled to TD. A low cement top was found when a cement bond log was run. Perforations were shot in the production casing at (4,430) and (6,000) feet. Cement was pumped into the production casing and through the cement retainer. The cement retainer didn't hold in the production casing. The cement retainer was drilled out. Diesel based drilling mud overflowed the 12H well casing vent tank onto containment. Some of the mud got outside the containment. The mud came out of the top of the tank in the form of a flow, then rolled off the containment to the pad surface, and then it flowed under the containment. The spill volume is over (5) gallons, but may be under (42). We may be able to calculate the volume of the spill, and determine it is under (42) gallons. The spill happened around 5 PM yesterday. Marlon Droddy, the site company man found the spill and reported it to Mike Cromley, the site safety man. Remediation of the impacted area started last night. Initially, we were not able to dig under the vent lines. We eventually moved the vent tanks and the containment to evaluate the extent of the impact.” Resource Environmental provided the following information relevant to remediation of the impacted area. “We arrived here today at 9AM. A small excavation of the impacted area was done yesterday. The excavation is now at (5) feet below the ground surface of the pad. Three test pits have been dug to determine the extent of the impact. The test pits were excavated and backfilled North, South, and just next to the impacted area. The test pits were excavated to a depth of (5) feet. Visually impacted material was not observed in the test pits. The PID meter didn't detect any readings in the test pits. Initial PID reading of soil in the impacted area was (592) parts per million (PPM). The PID reading in the vent tank was (741) PPM. We use (25) PPM as a standard threshold. In addition to using a PID meter to guide the remediation, we will use visual and olfactory senses.” Steve Catalfamo of Cabot indicated impacted material will most likely be transported for disposal to Alliance Landfill in Taylor, PA, and Cabot will attempt to determine the volume of the spill. The Department left the site at 14:20.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/22/2021 to ARD OPR LLC in Cascade Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARD OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/22/2021
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 911114
Permit API: 081-21802
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/22/2021
Comments: An incident inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that produced water was released from a GPU dump line. The report stated that on Saturday, March 20, 2021, a crew monitoring the wells remotely noticed erratic gauge trends and the volume of the release was initially estimated at 1 to 5 barrels in this notification. I met with ARD representative Rick Hall on location. Mr. Hall told me that a failed valve on the 10H well GPU led to a release of 12 barrels of produced water to the pad surface. He said that they believe that the GPU dump line sprayed produced water inside the double-walled GPU for 2 hours and since the well produces an average of 12 barrels of produced water per hour, the total volume released from the line was 24 barrels. The containment within the GPU held 12 barrels of produced water and 12 barrels overflowed to the pad surface. The 10H well was remotely shut-in after two hours of erratic gauge trends. Mr. Hall stated that ARD intends to pursue Act 2 remediation and they contracted an environmental consultant, GES, to oversee the process. A line of puddles is present along the west edge of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of these puddles is 8.35 mS/cm in the area closest to the 10H GPU and the EC in the puddles decreases steadily farther away. The GPU was moved to another area of the pad and in the small puddle on the pad where it had been staged, the EC was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. When I relayed my findings to Mr. Hall, he stated that on Saturday morning, the puddles along the west side of the pad were all below 1 mS/cm. I took a sample, ID# 0718-175, from the puddle along the west side of the pad where the EC is between 7.5 and 8.35 mS/cm, adjacent to the location where the 10H GPU had been staged. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Violations noted.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8207182
Permit API: 081-21812
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/06/2024
Comments: On November 6, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. Beech Resources reported a spill of approximately 210 barrels of produced fluid on the evening of November 5, 2024. Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. Mr. Stevenson said that a coupler failed on a freshwater pump connected to a Y fitting that blended with production fluid. When the failure happened the production fluid pump overtook the line and released the production fluid onto the well pad surface. The pad is being used as a staging area for the Delta Well Pad stimulation so there was already equipment onsite. Immediately, a vacuum truck began removing the free liquid off the well pad surface. Approximately half of the well pad surface was impacted by produced fluid spill. Beech Resources and their contractors worked through the night of November 5, 2024 to excavate and remove about 90 percent of the impacted surface. During the inspection, Penn E and R arrived onsite to screen the excavation for further impacted areas and collect Act 2 confirmatory samples. DEP broadly screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter and the range of conductivity in the excavation was 200 uS/cm to 2,000 uS/cm. Beech Resources plans to move the impacted soil into dumpsters and have it hauled off site. DEP did not observe any indication of the produced fluid leaving the well pad. Due to the production fluid spill onto the well pad surface violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted. Beech Resources plans to remediate the site through the Act 2 process.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 2019-04-16
Comments: An oil release to ground from a malfunctioning valve on the discharge pipe of one of the two tanks located in secondary containment at this well site was reported by Kenneth Fleeman on April 11, 2019. Oil was released from the tank by a malfunctioning valve which resulted in oil flow to the southwest end of the secondary containment where it disappeared into the stony soil. There is dead vegetation and oily pools of water observed to the east, south and west of the secondary containment. A 200 foot path of dead vegetation extends south of the well site. The path of dead vegetation disappears on the slope south of the well site and does not appear to have reached any waterways. A patch of dead vegetation and several oily pools of water is evident 15' east of the secondary containment. There is a 50' to 70' path of vegetation to the southwest however the oil does not appear to have moved any farther. Abarta Production Supervisor, Scott Patterson, stated that all tanks and piping were intact at the time of his inspection of the well on April 1, 2019 and the tank had approximately 13" of oil (10.75 barrels) at that time. All oil above the the discharge pipe was released to ground. Based on conductivity testing this was an oil release only, no brine was released. This is a violation of PA Oil and Gas Regulations and a clean-up process will be required. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Ashby 1H (A) well site located Athens Township, Bradford County on 4/5/2023 at 1030 hours. The weather was 63 degrees with partly cloudy skies. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID #371126 is tied to this release within CTS.On 4/4/2023 at ~1430 hours, a release of approximately 7 gallons of produced water occurred at the Ashby pad after a hose wasn't emptied prior to disconnecting from the offload valve of the produced water tank. The trucking company returned to the site and recovered the produced water on the surface but didn't fully recover all the impacted pad material. When I arrived onsite, pad material in the impacted area (photos #2 and 3) was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings of >4.00mS/cm. All standing water that I field measured for electrical conductivity on the pad surface returned readings ranging 400 to 700us/cm. On 4/5/2023, after remedial activities were completed, Blackhill Energy provided photographs confirming the clean-up to me via email.Based on the reported release of 7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface, violations of 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), 35 P.S. 6018.301, and 35 P.S. 691.402(b) are cited against API #015-21997. These violations will be cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED based on Blackhill Energy's timely remedial response.I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/17/2025
Comments: On October 17 2025 the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Gaut 4 Well Pad in regards to a spill reported to the Department at 9:23am on 10/17/2025 (CTS 393035). Present during the inspection was operator representative Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter showed the Department the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carpenter, the spill occurred around 8:00am on 10/17/2025. The spill of approximately 10 gallons of production fluid occurred from a flow line that ran from the wellhead to a gas buster unit. Upon observation of the spill the flow to the line was stopped. Mr. Carpenter stated that clean up crews were on route to remediate the spill. He stated that the gas buster and the secondary containment would be moved so all contaminated material could be removed. He stated that when reconnected, the gas buster and entire flowline would be in secondary containment to ensure another spill does not occur. He also stated that a valve would be added to the flow line so a pressure test could be conducted prior to using the line again.At the time of the inspection, the Department observed the location of the spill adjacent to the gas buster, below the flow line. Saturated/stained gravel was observed in this area. The spill appeared to be approximately 15 feet long by 10 feet wide. It appeared the contaminated area extended under the secondary containment for the gas buster unit. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the saturated/stained gravel with readings of 17.97mS, 17.50mS, and 5.60mS. It appeared the conductivity readings decreased with distance away from the flow line. A reading was taken just outside the saturated/stained gravel with a reading of 0.04mS. A background conductivity reading was taken away from the location of the spill with a reading of 0.05mS.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested to follow up on current onsite operations. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Violation Code: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8241978
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #3978563 conducted on May 15 2025 at 0848. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, or failure. While onsite the well appeared to be producing off of the 4" production string. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 94% combustible gas. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on July 24, 2025. The results were as follows: South and East slam bar holes: Non-detect for combustible gas. North slam bar hole: Peak reading of 3% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. West slam bar hole: Peaking reading of 18% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. Due to the lack of adequate sustained concentration, a viable sample for isotopic analysis could not be collected. On May 22, 2025 the Department received an email from the operator stating that "Titus would prefer to have the Johnson #1 well plugged". As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with it. The Department requests a detailed timeline specifying when the well will be properly plugged or when corrective measures will be undertaken to bring the well into full regulatory compliance.

Comments: On February 10, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. STL Resources is still awaiting sample results to be able to dispose of the soil to the landfill. The conductor rig was onsite in the process of drilling the second well cellar and conductor of four. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227 and 3306834.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/12/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8284379
Permit API: 123-46784
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) reported a release of produced fluids at TMP's Brown Hill Road tank battery. The tank battery consists of five 210 bbl stock tanks (# 1053, 1054, 1055, 1056, 1057), a separator, gas meter, burner, and buried brine tank. The Brown Hill Church Lease, Lyszaz Lease, and R Brown Lease are plumbed to this tank battery.It was reported that lightning from recent thunderstorms must have struck the tanks, ignited combustible contents, and caused an explosion that expanded and ruptured four out of the five tanks. The released fluid flowed through the ruptures and into the secondary containment area. It was reported that at the time of the release, the stock tanks were mostly empty but did contain some sludge from prior storage of produced fluids.Brian Bennett of TMP was onsite at the time of this inspection to discuss cleanup expectations with Evan Bruce (WQS) and I (Mathew Haemer - WQS). Brian estimated that the volume of the released fluids was approximately 4 bbl. Brian explained that he had been working on mixing sawdust with the sludge that had filled the containment area and had begun to remove the saturated sawdust to temporary storage in barrels staged inside the secondary containment area.At the time of this inspection, the buried brine tank was nearly empty. The majority of the release pooled around the buried brine tank. Brine was not reported to be a suspected component of this release. However, elevated SPC readings were observed both in the sawdust/sludge mixture (5,350 uS/cm) and in the soils of the secondary containment area's western end (8,900 uS/cm).Two groundhog holes were observed in the northwest corner of the secondary containment area. Elevated SPC readings (4,140/12,250 uS/cm) were observed in the soil inside of the groundhog holes. This indicates that at one point in time, brine discharged into the secondary containment area rose to a level sufficient to spill over into the holes, and from that point migrate outside of containment. A storage yard has been constructed downslope of the tank battery. HDPE pipe is scattered at one end, and spare pump jacks at the other. Coincidentally, the soil is visibly wet beneath the area where the HDPE pipe is scattered. Elevated SPC of soils (1,468 uS/cm) was observed where the pipe is scattered. The disturbed earth above the pipe and pump jacks also had elevated SPC readings (1,346 uS/cm). A violation for failure to construct and maintain a method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112 is being cited due to the evidence that brine was able to migrate through the secondary containment wall via the groundhog holes and/or through permeating the earthen containment.The quantity of the release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold set forth in the Department's spill policy, therefore either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required. It is requested that the source and extent of the release be identified.
